candidates: When a function's signature changes (e.g., a callback parameter is removed, the calling convention switches from callback-based to promise-based), update all JSDoc for that function: remove or rewrite stale @param entries for deleted parameters, and update any inline code examples so they compile and run correctly against the new API. Do not leave callback-style examples or phantom @param docs after the API has changed.

When a public function serializes concurrent calls through an execution queue (e.g., multiple callers' promises are enqueued and resolved one at a time), document this concurrency behavior explicitly in the JSDoc using a @remarks block, so callers understand that simultaneous invocations are run serially rather than in parallel.
